name: Susama Dash/ସୁଷମା ଦାଶ୍

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Susama Dash’s poems in Kabita Live move between intimate encounter and public catastrophe. In “ଭେଟ”, a meeting revives a parched inner world: touch becomes rain, old dreams put out leaves, and warmth begins to dissolve accumulated hurt. The poem holds that renewal beside the hesitation of two people who cannot easily speak everything they feel.

“ଯୁଦ୍ଧ” turns from the private room towards a city shaken by bombs. Images of fire, detained innocents and a throne raised above bones expose the human cost of conquest. A bird seeking peace and a mother’s cry shift attention from power to vulnerable lives. The brief captured text of “ଆର୍ଯ୍ୟପୁତ୍ର” returns to a quieter question: where can two people go to escape the crowd?
